value: You must finish your homework before playing.

value: She is the best dancer in the class.

We use "at" with an exact clock time, so "at 5 o'clock" is correct. The others should be "in the evening", "on Monday" and "at 8 o'clock".

value: She had finished her homework before dinner.

value: He is not going to the park, but she is going.
reasoning: "He is not going" is negative and "she is going" is affirmative, so sentence A has one of each. B has two negative clauses, while C and D have two affirmative clauses.
The blank is part of the subject (the people who went), so we need the subject pronoun "I": John and I went to the park. "Me", "him" and "her" are object pronouns.

value: The rabbit is faster than the turtle.

value: The chair was placed next to the table in the room.
reasoning: Neuter gender nouns name non-living things that are neither male nor female, such as chair, table and room. The other sentences are about people or animals.

value: The teacher spoke to him after class.

"Team" is the name for a group of players taken as one unit, so it is a collective noun.
An adverb of manner tells how something is done and often ends in "-ly". The girl sang loudly. "Loud" is an adjective, "sing" is a verb and "song" is a noun.

value: The lesson was explained by the teacher, and the assignment was completed by students.

value: I finish my homework hardly before dinner each day.

value: John said that he would meet me at the library the next day.

value: She went to bed because she was tired.

value: They have been to the museum three times this month.
